description: Combining increases bleeding risk significantly; both affect blood clotting.
NSAIDs like ibuprofen can increase bleeding risk when combined with warfarin.
Alcohol can increase the risk of lactic acidosis when combined with metformin.
NSAIDs may reduce the blood-pressure-lowering effect of ACE inhibitors and affect kidney function.
Combining increases risk of serotonin syndrome.
Combining beta-blockers with certain calcium channel blockers can cause dangerously low heart rate/blood pressure.
Calcium can reduce absorption of levothyroxine; space doses apart by several hours.
Combining increases risk of dangerously high potassium levels (hyperkalemia).
Omeprazole may reduce the antiplatelet effectiveness of clopidogrel.

Alcohol can increase the risk of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) when combined with insulin.
Regular ibuprofen use may reduce the cardioprotective antiplatelet effect of low-dose aspirin.
